- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., 0.33 → 0.67 or vice versa), model misreads momentum; adjust forecast by smoothing transition over 2–3 days.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show high volatility, forecast should trend toward historical mean (last 18-day avg) by day 7–10.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights short-term sentiment; if sentiment is positive for 5+ days, reduce forecast slope to reflect diminishing momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently low (0.00 or negative) and price is rising, model may misread trend; treat as “false breakout” and reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
